skill.name: mcp-integration
skill.description: Guides users through configuring Model Context Protocol servers in Claude Code plugins, including local stdio servers, hosted endpoints, authentication, tool naming, testing, and security practices.
skill.summary: Configure MCP servers and tools for Claude Code plugins.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static findings are expected documentation examples for MCP endpoints, environment-variable placeholders, and shell snippets. They do not execute code, include live secrets, or show data-exfiltration intent. No prompt injection attempts or hidden malicious instructions were found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders clearly marked and continue warning users not to commit .env files or hardcode tokens.

remediation.issue: Stdio MCP servers can execute local processes when users adopt a configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Emphasize trusted server packages, pinned dependencies, and least-privilege filesystem paths.

remediation.issue: Dynamic header helper examples use shell commands for token handling.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend vetted helper scripts, restrictive file permissions, and secret-manager based token retrieval.

static_findings.snippet: Connect to RESTful MCP servers via standard HTTP requests. Best for token-based auth and stateless i
Use `/mcp` command to see all servers including plugin-provided ones.

- **`references/tool-usage.md`** - Using MCP tools in commands and agents

- Claude Code spawns and manages the process

content.user_title: Configure MCP Servers for AI Plugins
content.value_statement: Developers need reliable steps for connecting Claude Code plugins to external tools and services. This skill provides MCP configuration patterns, authentication guidance, and testing practices.
actual_capabilities: Covers stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket MCP transports.
Shows environment variable substitution for tokens and plugin paths.
Describes MCP tool naming and allowed-tools frontmatter.
Provides troubleshooting steps for connection, authentication, and tool errors.
Includes example patterns for local, hosted, and REST-based MCP servers.
limitations: Does not install or validate real MCP servers by itself.
Example URLs and credentials must be replaced before use.
Focuses on Claude Code plugins, not every MCP client.
Security depends on the chosen server, scopes, and local environment.

use_cases.title: Add a Hosted Service
use_cases.description: Configure an SSE or HTTP MCP endpoint with OAuth or token-based authentication.

use_cases.title: Bundle a Local Server
use_cases.description: Package a stdio MCP server with portable paths and documented environment variables.

use_cases.title: Review MCP Permissions
use_cases.description: Check tool naming, allowed-tools entries, authentication scopes, and testing coverage before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a hosted MCP service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a hosted MCP server to my Claude Code plugin. Ask for the service URL, auth method, and tool names first.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Config
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing plugin configuration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my existing .mcp.json for portability, authentication, and HTTPS usage. Explain required changes before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Service Tools
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design for coordinated external services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-server MCP integration for GitHub and Jira workflows. Use specific allowed tools and avoid wildcard permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Secure Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for sensitive local and cloud resources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a secure MCP integration plan for a plugin that uses a local database server and a cloud API. Include testing and failure handling.

output_examples.input: Add an Asana MCP server to a plugin.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with the server type, OAuth flow, expected tool names, required tests, and README updates.

output_examples.input: Review my MCP configuration for security issues.
output_examples.output: A short review covering HTTPS use, secret handling, filesystem scope, tool permissions, and missing documentation.

output_examples.input: Create a troubleshooting guide for failed MCP connections.
output_examples.output: A checklist for URL validation, authentication state, server startup, tool discovery, debug logs, and user-facing errors.

best_practices: Use environment variables or OAuth flows for secrets, never hardcode tokens.
Prefer HTTPS or WSS endpoints and verify URLs before publishing plugin config.
Pre-allow only required MCP tools and document each permission.
anti_patterns: Using wildcard MCP tool permissions for routine commands.
Committing .env files, real tokens, or database passwords with plugin examples.
Running stdio servers from untrusted commands or user-controlled paths.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps configure MCP servers for Claude Code plugins that connect to APIs, databases, local tools, and hosted services.

faq.question: Can it configure local and hosted MCP servers?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers stdio, SSE, HTTP, and WebSocket transports with different authentication patterns.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets for me?
faq.answer: No. It explains environment variables and OAuth patterns, but users must manage secrets securely.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: It is focused on Claude Code plugins. Many MCP concepts still apply to other clients.

faq.question: Can Codex use this guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the steps to plan, review, or edit MCP plugin configuration.

faq.question: What should I verify before publishing?
faq.answer: Verify endpoints, environment variables, least-privilege tool access, authentication scopes, tests, and error handling.
